question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
sql:
-- Final check - verify the monthly totals
WITH date_range AS (
  SELECT customer_id,
    CAST(MIN(txn_date) AS DATE) as earliest,
    CAST(MAX(txn_date) AS DATE) as latest
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
all_dates AS (
  SELECT customer_id,
    earliest,
    latest,
    (earliest + INTERVAL (row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) - 1) DAY) as cal_date
  FROM date_range
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT unnest(generate_series(0, CAST(latest AS DATE) - CAST(earliest AS DATE))) as day_offset
  )
),
txn_daily AS (
  SELECT customer_id,
    CAST(txn_date AS DATE) as txn_date,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) as daily_net
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, CAST(txn_date AS DATE)
),
daily_balances AS (
  SELECT ad.customer_id,
    ad.cal_date,
    SUM(COALESCE(td.daily_net, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY ad.customer_id ORDER BY ad.cal_date ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) as balance
  FROM all_dates ad
  LEFT JOIN txn_daily td ON ad.customer_id = td.customer_id AND ad.cal_date = td.txn_date
),
daily_balances_floor AS (
  SELECT customer_id,
    cal_date,
    GREATEST(balance, 0) as daily_balance
  FROM daily_balances
),
monthly_max AS (
  SELECT customer_id,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', cal_date) as month,
    MAX(daily_balance) as max_daily_balance
  FROM daily_balances_floor
  GROUP BY customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', cal_date)
)
SELECT month,
  SUM(max_daily_balance) as monthly_total
FROM monthly_max
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
